name: E-mu Emax
source: E-mu Systems 'EMAX MIDI and RS-422 specs', Copyright E-MU Systems 1986, 'Valid for EMAX Software Rev. 3.0', 12/16/86 (27 pp., Emulator Archive transcription; http://www.emulatorarchive.com/assets/PDF/Emax%20MIDI.pdf via web.archive.org): implementation chart, transmitted/received basic and system exclusive messages, MMA sample dump, Supermode, realtime controllers, voice parameter list (p.24) and preset parameter list. Emax Owner's Manual v2.0 (Craig Anderton, 1986; Emulator Archive 2001 edition, vintagesynth.com/sites/default/files/2017-05/EmaxManual.pdf): panel ranges/scaling (Analog Processing 00-22, Preset Definition 1-9, Master 1-8, Sample 3-4), keyboard numbering, MIDI chart ('System exclusives: call for documentation'). Emax Service Manual 1987 (archive.org e-mu_systems_emax_service_manual_searchable): MIDI/RS-422 interface, OS overlays from floppy, 16 x 41256 sound RAM, E-chip ~2:1 compression. Hardware-tested #1A examples: micromoog on sequencer.de 'Emulator II & Emax I User aufgepasst' (2010). OS history: Emulator Archive OS list (nonaudio.wordpress.com mirror). SDS support list: dissidents.com Sample Wrench FAQ ('SDS 12 Bit: E-Mu EMax').

emax.noChannel: E-mu exclusives carry NO channel and NO device ID: F0 18 02 <cmd> <data> F7. Every Emax on the cable answers. There is no SysEx on/off switch in the Rev 3.0 spec or the manual. (MMA Sample Dump messages F0 7E <cc> ... do carry a channel byte.)
emax.numbers: All bytes hex unless noted; parameter numbers in the spec's lists are DECIMAL (VCF decay = 41 = 29h, cutoff = 31 = 1Fh -- confirmed by the hardware examples).
emax.keyNumbers: key# 0-87 = MIDI note 21-108 (A-1..C7 in E-mu naming, middle C = C3 = key 39 = note 60). The 61-note keyboard spans C1-C6 = key 15-75 = note 36-96. options arrays here use key# order.
emax.levels: 0 = primary voice, 1 = secondary voice, 2 = both (only #1A, #11, #13 accept 2).
emax.multiByte: 19-bit sample values travel as 3 bytes, 7 bits each, LEAST significant group first: [v & 7F, (v >> 7) & 7F, (v >> 14) & 1F].

miscInfo.reply: F0 18 02 32 <current preset> <master tune 0-31> <flags> <soundRAM 3 bytes LSB-group first> <presetRAM 3 bytes> <16 ASCII chars software rev> F7

sampleInfo.reply: F0 18 02 33 <key> <level> <rate 0-7> <length x3> <sus start x3> <sus end x3> <rel start x3> <rel end x3> <flags: b0 loop on, b1 loop in release, b2 backwards> F7

crossfadeInfo.reply: F0 18 02 34 <key> <b0-2 mode, b3 0=primary hard 1=secondary hard> <positional start key> <# keys in positional section - 1> F7

ready.note: 'Provided as a means for an external device to find out if EMAX is present' -- the probe.

voiceParam.note: current preset; every voice touching lo..hi; null voice = ignored; no range checks

sampleInfo.send: F0 18 02 1C <key> <level> <rate> <sus start x3> <sus end x3> <rel start x3> <rel end x3> <flags> F7
sampleInfo.note: all fields at once (no length); build from the last #33 read

editAssignment.send: F0 18 02 12 <level 0/1> <key> <new orig key> <new lo key> <new hi key> <lo ch 0-7> <hi ch 0-7> F7

crossfade.send: F0 18 02 14 <lo key> <hi key> <dir 0=pri hard 1=sec hard> <mode 0-5> F7

currentPreset.note: like program change but bypasses omni/poly and MIDI-enable checks; a nonexistent preset is ignored

copyPreset.note: 'to' may not be the current preset. RAM only.

timeout.note: sample-dump handshake timeout, default 4 s, until power-off

neverSend.1D: Erase All -- wipes every preset, voice, sample and sequence in RAM
neverSend.10: Load Bank from disk -- replaces the whole RAM bank (disk is only read)
neverSend.15: Create Preset -- overwrites an existing preset of that number
neverSend.07/18/19: 'Fast' sample transfers: the Emax switches its port to 500 kbaud synchronous, which is RS-422 only -- useless over MIDI (it waits, then errors)
neverSend.11: Execute Get Voice (copy voices between presets; no range checks) -- not needed by the editor

emax.readyHandshake: After every Change/Execute command (#1A, #1B, #1C, #12, #14, #17, #1E, #21, #22 ...) the Emax sends READY F0 18 02 38 F7 when done; the spec says 'Sender should wait for this signal before sending more commands.' Requests are answered directly with their #3x reply. So the transport is one message in flight at a time: send, wait for the reply/READY (timeout), send the next.
emax.noDiskWrite: No SysEx writes to disk. Everything written lands in the RAM bank and is lost at power-off unless saved on the panel (PRESET MANAGEMENT 2 Save All, or per-preset save).
emax.noBulkDump: There is no whole-preset or whole-bank parameter dump: a preset is read parameter by parameter (#01 x 52 used param numbers), plus per-voice #00 x 46, #03, #04 and the two key maps.

examples.what: read primary filter cutoff of the voice on C3 (key 39 = 27h, param 31 = 1Fh)
cutoff = 80 (50h) on both layers of every voice in the preset (the circulated, hardware-used example)
VCF decay = 20 on every voice (micromoog's example)
pitch bend range +-2 on the current preset (param 61 = 3Dh)

examples.alt: C<ch> 0C (always received, but the omni/poly channel test applies)

examples.what: sample info of primary voice on C3, length 100000 words

params.name: Edit Target Low Key
params.note: Driver state, never sent as a parameter. The key whose voice (per level) is READ, and the low end of the key range every voice-level WRITE targets (#1A lo key). Mirrors the panel's ANALOG PROCESSING 00 'Select Lo Voice'. Changing it re-reads the voice params at that key.

params.name: Edit Target High Key
params.note: Driver state. High end of the write range (#1A hi key); driver uses max(editLo, editHi). Every voice with any key inside lo..hi is changed (manual AP 00: 'if the range includes part of a Voice, the entire Voice will be processed'). editLo=A-1 + editHi=C7 = whole keyboard, like pressing ANALOG PROCESSING twice.

params.name: Pri VCA Hold

params.name: Pri VCA Decay

params.name: Pri VCA Release

params.name: Pri Voice Tuning

params.name: Pri Output Channel Low

params.name: Pri Voice # at edit key
params.note: From the primary voice map (request #05, reply #35: 88 bytes, one voice # per key). 127 = no voice on that key. Map numbers are not the LCD's voice numbers but correspond one-to-one.

params.name: Pri Voice Low Key
params.note: Read: first key of the run of keys that holds the edit key's voice # in the map. Write: #12 Execute Edit Assignment (level, key, orig, lo, hi, lo ch, hi ch) -- the Emax does NO range checks; an overlapping or over-transposed range can overwrite neighbours. Sent only on an explicit edit, never by sendPatch.

params.name: Pri Voice High Key
params.note: Last key of that run. Written with #12 as above.

params.name: Sec Voice # at edit key
params.note: From the secondary voice map (request #06, reply #36: 88 bytes, one voice # per key). 127 = no voice on that key. Map numbers are not the LCD's voice numbers but correspond one-to-one.

params.name: MIDI Basic Channel
params.note: Per preset. Notes / program change are received (Poly) and transmitted on it. SysEx carries no channel, so this never cuts the editor off, but notes sent on another channel go unheard in Poly mode.

params.name: MIDI Notes/Wheels
params.note: 0 = ignore/transmit no notes or wheels (clock only). Keep 1 for the record pipeline.

params.name: Preset Change Enabled
params.note: Only gates TRANSMITTING program changes; received ones are always obeyed (spec).

params.name: MIDI Port
params.note: DANGER: 0 = THRU turns the MIDI OUT jack into a thru, so the Emax's SysEx replies and READYs stop reaching the editor. Per preset: every preset the editor selects must be 'out'. The driver refuses to write 0.

params.note: 16-bit value split over preset params 46 (bits 0-1), 47 (bits 2-8), 48 (bits 9-15): value = p46 | p47 << 2 | p48 << 9. Range 4000-24000 = the panel's 40.00-240.00 BPM (hundredths of a BPM, inferred). Write all three parts.

params.name: Arpeggiator Note Value
params.note: Order taken from the manual's list (PRESET DEFINITION 6; 1/16 is the default); code mapping inferred.

params.name: Arpeggiator Key Repeats

params.name: Cruz Control
params.note: Turning it on turns key repeats and glissando off (panel).

params.name: Arpeggiator Interval
params.note: Raw 0-15. The panel lists m2 M2 m3 M3 P4 m5 P5 m6 M6 m7 m9 M9 Oct m10 M10 (15 names for 16 codes) -- code-to-name mapping unknown.

params.name: Arpeggiator Velocity
params.note: 0 = 'played' (each note keeps its played velocity).

params.name: Pitch Bend Range
params.note: Semitones. 0 is invalid -- never send it.

params.name: Velocity Curve
params.note: Panel 01-14; 14 (raw 13) = fixed dynamics. Stored per preset (manual MASTER 3).

params.name: Arpeggiator Harmony 1
params.note: 0 = off (inferred); otherwise an interval m2..M10.

params.name: Master Tune
params.note: Whole instrument, not saved per preset. 16 = 0; 3 cents per step (MASTER 1: +45..-48 cents). Spec bug note: on Rev 3.0 values 0-15 (flat) 'don't work properly'.

params.name: Super Mode
params.note: 16-channel multitimbral via the sequencer track presets. Leave off for the editor.

params.name: MIDI Overflow
params.note: On = notes beyond 8 voices go out MIDI instead of stealing. Leave off.

banks.label: presets
banks.note: P00-P99 in the RAM bank (whatever the loaded disk holds; empty numbers read name char 1 = 0). Selecting sends #1E (or PC) and makes it the current preset -- the one all voice edits land on. Read = preset-level params only (#01 pp, no selection needed). 'write' = RAM only: into the current preset directly, or Execute Copy Preset (#17 current -> prog) for another slot, overwriting it in RAM. Nothing reaches the floppy: save on the panel (PRESET MANAGEMENT 2).

programs.note: One bank of 100 presets (0-99), all RAM, loaded from floppy. Program Change 0-99 on the preset's basic channel is always obeyed (the panel's 'Preset Change' switch only gates transmitting). No bank select. The edit focus inside a preset is a VOICE, addressed by key + level (editLo/editHi + layer select), not a program slot.

areas.what: all preset-level params of presets 0-99 (names, routing, MIDI, arp, bend, velocity curve)
areas.request: F0 18 02 01 <pp> <param#> F7 per param (52 used param numbers x existing presets)

areas.what: voice-level params of every voice of one preset
areas.request: make it current (#1E), #05 + #06 maps, then per voice (one key per map run, both levels) #00 key L param# x 46, #03, #04

areas.what: global misc info (master tune, supermode, overflow, arp clock, RAM free, OS string)

areas.request: SDS dump request F0 7E cc 03 key level F7 per voice (slow: ~20 s per second of audio)

backup.notInSysex: No bulk dump exists and the voice/preset STRUCTURE (which voices exist, key maps, dual-voice mode) can only be recreated by panel work or by SDS placement + #12 assignment. The real backup is the floppy itself: image the bank disks (Gotek/HxC, or the EMXP tool that reads Emax disk images). The SysEx parameter snapshot is a record + restore of parameter values onto the same bank.
backup.restore: Load the same bank from disk, then replay the recorded #1B / #1A / #1C writes (one at a time, READY each). Save to disk on the panel.

setup: OS: boot a Rev 3.x Emax OS disk (the SysEx spec used here is 'Valid for EMAX Software Rev. 3.0', 12/16/86; 3.2 of 04/10/87 is the final non-HD/non-SE release). OS 2.x (the launch releases) may lack some commands -- check MASTER 8 > 7 Software Revision, or the editor's #02 reply. SE/HD/Plus units run their own OS lines (SE 1.1, HD 1.1, Plus 1.0); this schema was written from the non-SE 3.0 spec.

Load a bank (LOAD ALL + ENTER) and LEAVE the disk (or Gotek image) in the drive: the Emax pages parts of its OS in from the floppy as modules are used (service manual), and the manual says there must be a disk in the drive when any module is activated.
Cable both ways: interface out -> Emax MIDI IN; Emax MIDI OUT -> interface in. Replies and every READY come back on MIDI OUT.

PRESET DEFINITION 7 (MIDI Setup) in the preset you will edit: MIDI Port = Out (NOT Thru -- Thru stops the replies), Notes/Wheels = yes, mode Poly with Basic Channel = the editor channel (or Omni). These are per preset: check each preset you switch to.
MASTER 8 (Special) > 2 MIDI Overflow = off, and SEQUENCER SETUP 6 Super Mode = off, so notes you send land on the current preset.
Stay on the preset-select screen (no module active, sequencer stopped, not sampling) while the editor works. Behaviour of SysEx while a panel module is mid-dialog is not documented.
There is no SysEx enable or device ID to set. With two Emaxes on one MIDI cable both obey every E-mu SysEx message.
Keep it: everything the editor writes is RAM. Save on the panel (PRESET MANAGEMENT 2 Save All) to a disk you mean to overwrite -- ideally a copy/Gotek image of the original bank.

sampleTransfer.summary: YES, over MIDI: the Emax I speaks the MMA MIDI Sample Dump Standard in both directions at 12 bits (spec 'MMA Sample Dump Commands'; dissidents' Sample Wrench list: 'SDS 12 Bit: E-Mu EMax'). The spec's proprietary 'fast' transfers (#07 send, #18 accept, #19 replace) run at 500 kbaud synchronous = RS-422 port only; not usable from a MIDI interface.
sampleTransfer.sampleNumber: SDS sample number = 2 bytes (LSB, MSB): LSB = key# 0-87, MSB = level (0 primary, 1 secondary), i.e. number = key + 128 x level. Voices are addressed by key in the CURRENT preset. (For comparison the Emax II docs put secondary voices at 256 + key -- a different model; unverified for the Emax I beyond this spec.)
sampleTransfer.channelByte: F0 7E <cc> ...: spec calls it 'midi base channel (0 to 15)'. Use the current preset's MIDI basic channel (preset param 32, read with #01 7F 20). Whether the Emax rejects a mismatching cc is not stated.
upload: Pre-flight: #02 misc info -> sound RAM remaining (bytes ~ sample words; empty bank = 524288, manual MASTER 2). The Emax accepts a dump only if length <= remaining AND the current preset is not empty; it does not count memory that erasing would free.

Make sure the current preset exists: pick an empty number (#01 pp 00 -> 0), create it on the panel (PRESET MANAGEMENT 3) or with #15 pp -- #15 OVERWRITES an existing preset, so only on a verified-empty number -- then #1E pp.

Header: F0 7E cc 01 <key> <level> 0C <period ns x3, LSB group first> <length words x3> <sus loop start x3> <sus loop end x3> <loop type, ignored> F7. Example, 1 s at 27.778 kHz on C3 primary: F0 7E 00 01 27 00 0C 20 19 02 02 59 01 00 00 00 01 59 01 00 F7 (period 36000 ns = 20 19 02; length 27778 = 02 59 01; loop end 27777 = 01 59 01).
The Emax answers WAIT (F0 7E cc 7C pp F7) while it decides, then ACK (7F) to accept or CANCEL (7D) to refuse (no room / empty current preset).

Packets: F0 7E cc 02 <packet # 0-127, wraps> <120 data bytes> <checksum> F7 = 127 bytes, 60 words each; checksum = XOR of 7E, cc, 02, packet #, and the 120 data bytes, & 7F. Wait for ACK after each; NAK -> resend (the Emax tolerates 5 resends, then CANCEL); the last packet is ACKed too. Pad the final packet with zero-level words.

12-bit word packing (spec, standard SDS): w = unsigned 12-bit (signed s12 + 2048; 800h = silence); byte 0 = w >> 5 (7 MSBs), byte 1 = (w & 1F) << 2. 16-bit headers are also accepted ('packed according to the significant bits'), but cost 3 bytes/word -- quantize to 12 bits host-side and send 2 bytes/word.

After the dump the Emax: places the sample on that one key only (no transpose range), uses forward looping only (loop type ignored), rounds the period to the nearest internal rate (10, 15.625, 20, 22.05, 27.78, 31.25, 41.667, 44.1 kHz), and replaces the first two and last two words with zero -- pad both ends with two zero words and keep loops off them.

Then shape it with the editor's own messages: #1C loops/flags, #1A voice params (open the filter: cutoff 120, Q 0, env amt 50; VCA A 0, H 0, D 31, S 31, R ~4), and optionally #12 to widen the key range (no range checks -- keep the original key where it was placed).
sampleTransfer.download: F0 7E cc 03 <key> <level> F7 (Sample Dump Request) -> Emax sends header 01 (12 significant bits, period, length, sustain loop, loop type 0 fwd / 1 bkwd-fwd) then 02 packets; the host ACKs each (standard SDS handshake). Words are unsigned 12-bit as above. A null voice -> presumably no dump (not stated for SDS; the fast variant sends length 0).
sampleTransfer.memory: Sound memory = 16 x 41256 DRAM = 524288 bytes (service manual p.30; MASTER 2 shows SampleMem 524288 on an empty bank). The E-chip stores audio with a ~2:1 lossy compression 'into an average of 8 bits per sample' behind 12-bit converters (service manual p.42) -- so 524288 ~ sample words: 18.8 s at 27.778 kHz, 12.4 s at 41.667 kHz, 52 s at 10 kHz (manual SAMPLE 4 table). Samples sent over SDS are re-compressed by the E-chip: expect the Emax character, not a clean 12-bit copy.
sampleTransfer.speed: MIDI wire max 3125 bytes/s; one 60-word packet = 127 bytes = 40.6 ms plus the ACK turnaround -> roughly 1300-1450 words/s. 1 s of 27.778 kHz audio ~ 20-22 s; a full memory ~ 6-7 min. The fast RS-422 path would be ~16x faster but needs RS-422 hardware.
sampleTransfer.crushPipeline: For 'send a folder of WAVs -> play -> record the analog out': per WAV sum to mono, resample to an Emax rate (27.778 kHz = the Emax's 'good compromise', 41.667 kHz for more top, 10 or 15.625 kHz for grit), quantize to 12-bit (truncate/no dither for the grittier sound), add 2 zero words at each end, SDS it to one key of a scratch preset (key k, primary), set loops/voice params, then play MIDI note k+21 on the preset's basic channel (C3 = key 39 = note 60 plays at original pitch) and record the stereo or that channel's individual output. Batch: fill up to ~18 s per load at 27.778 kHz across keys 0-87 (primary; secondary level doubles key slots), render, clear the scratch preset on the panel (or erase-voice, which the editor will not send), repeat. Budget ~20 s of transfer per second of audio.
gotchas: Current preset must exist and be the target: SDS lands in the CURRENT preset only.
Memory check ignores space freed by erasing -- delete on the panel, then re-check #02.
The first and last two words become zero.
Keep MIDI Port = out in that preset (param 38) or ACKs never come back.
Uploads live in RAM; power-off loses them unless saved to disk on the panel.

driverNotes: NEW transport 'emax' (no driver yet -- add to drivers.js TRANSPORTS/makeDriver). Everything below is from the E-mu 'EMAX MIDI and RS-422 specs' (Rev 3.0, 12/16/86) unless marked. (1) FRAMING: every E-mu message is F0 18 02 <cmd> ... F7 with no channel/device byte. Match replies by cmd (30-38) plus echoed key/level/param#. Only one request or change in flight at a time: queue everything; after a request wait for its reply (timeout ~300 ms, 1000 ms for the first message after connect -- the OS pages program overlays in from the floppy, service manual p.30), after a change wait for READY F0 18 02 38 F7 (timeout ~500 ms; on timeout log and continue). gapMs 20 between messages. (2) EDIT MODEL (like the S-330): no edit buffer. The CURRENT PRESET is edited in place in RAM. Voice-level params (msg 'voice', 'sample', 'xfade', 'assign', 'map') always refer to the current preset; preset-level params (msg 'preset') can address any preset (preset byte = 0-99 or 7F = current). The voice being edited is addressed by KEY, not by voice number: driver state editLo/editHi (msg 'local' params) plus the level from the param (p* = 0, s* = 1). Reads use key = editLo; writes use lo = editLo, hi = max(editLo, editHi). When the layout's layer select is 'both', the editor sends the p* and s* param one after another -- the driver may merge a pair of identical p/s writes into one #1A with level 2. sendParam for editLo/editHi sends nothing; it stores the value (prefs 'editLo'/'editHi') and triggers a re-read of the voice-level params (requestPatch). (3) requestPatch(): (a) #02 misc info -> current preset #, master tune/flags, RAM free, software rev (keep for the rack card); (b) #05 and #06 key maps -> pVoice/sVoice at editLo, and pLoKey/pHiKey (sLoKey/sHiKey) = bounds of the run of keys around editLo that carry the same voice # (skip a level whose voice # is 7F); (c) for each level with a voice: #00 editLo L num for every msg 'voice' param (46 each), #03 editLo L (sample info), then #04 editLo (crossfade); (d) #01 7F num for every msg 'preset' param (52 param numbers incl. the 3 arpTempo parts). ~150 round trips, 9-byte messages: expect 2-5 s. Return { values, syx } where syx = the concatenated replies (a restorable record). Mirror all raw replies (sample info and assignment writes need the untouched fields). (4) VALUES: plain params: value = raw byte (min/max are raw; valueOffset/options are display only). bit fields: 'bit' (single flag) or 'bits' {shift,width} inside the misc flags byte or the sample flags byte. arpTempo: 'parts' [{num,width,at}] -> value = sum(part << at); write every part. msg 'sample' field rate/susStart/susEnd/relStart/relEnd/flags/length map to reply #33 positions; 19-bit fields per emax.multiByte. xfade: mode = byte & 7, dir = (byte >> 3) & 1. (5) sendParam(p, v): readOnly -> ignore. 'voice' -> F0 18 02 1A lo hi L num v F7 (+READY). 'preset' -> F0 18 02 1B 7F num v F7. 'sample' -> rebuild the full #1C from the #33 mirror with this field replaced (refuse if that level was never read). 'xfade' -> F0 18 02 14 lo hi dir mode F7 from the mirror. 'assign' -> F0 18 02 12 L editLo orig lo hi loCh hiCh F7 from the mirror + new lo/hi (confirm in the UI first: no range checks, can overwrite neighbouring voices), then re-read the maps. 'misc' -> F0 18 02 22 tune flags F7 from the mirror. Coalesce: while a message is queued keep only the newest value per param. Refuse midiPort = 0 (thru) and bendRange = 0. Edits take effect on the NEXT note-on (manual: 'You must re-trigger a note to hear any changes'); held notes do not change -- fine for the play-and-record pipeline, not a real-time modulation path (forum users report the same). (6) sendPatch(values): write every modelled, non-readOnly, non-'assign' param that differs from the mirror (voice params to editLo..editHi, preset params to 7F), one at a time with READY. Refuse before a successful requestPatch (mirror empty). (7) programChange(bi, prog): F0 18 02 1E prog F7 (bypasses omni/poly; READY), then requestPatch. Fallback: C<ch> prog (spec: always received regardless of 'Preset Change On/Off'). A nonexistent preset leaves the current one unchanged -- check with #02. (8) requestProgram(bi, prog): preset-level params only, WITHOUT changing the current preset: #01 prog num for every msg 'preset' param. data = 69-entry array indexed by preset param # (unread = null), name = chars at 0,2..22, empty preset if param 0 = 0 (then skip the rest). Voice-level values are not available for a non-current preset. requestSlotName(bi, prog): 12 x #01 (just #01 prog 00 first; stop if 0). A 100-slot name scan is up to ~1200 round trips (~10-15 s): cache per session, forgetBank clears. (9) writeProgram(bi, prog, values) -- RAM ONLY: if prog = current preset: same as sendPatch. Otherwise the Emax cannot 'store' an edit buffer; use Execute Copy Preset F0 18 02 17 <current> <prog> F7 (+READY; the spec forbids to = current) which duplicates the current preset -- voices, assignments, preset params -- into slot prog in RAM, overwriting whatever preset prog held (confirm in the UI if requestSlotName(prog) is not empty); then #1B prog num v for each preset param in values that differs. Return the preset param array; verify with requestProgram(prog) + sameProgram. Tell the user: save to disk on the Emax panel (PRESET MANAGEMENT 2) or it is gone at power-off. (10) sameProgram(a, b): compare the preset-param arrays at modelled numbers (skip unused odd name slots). (11) probe(): send F0 18 02 08 F7, wait 1000 ms for F0 18 02 38 F7; then #02 for the software revision string. (12) decode(ev): the Emax does not transmit parameter edits made on its panel (voice/preset params are sent only on request). It does transmit Program Change C<basic ch> pp when the preset is changed on the panel (if Preset Change is enabled in that preset) -> treat as 'current preset changed': re-run requestPatch. Ignore unsolicited READYs. (13) SAFETY: never send the commands in emax.neverSend. Never let a queued write outlive a preset change (flush the queue before #1E). The editor never touches the floppy.
uncertain: Primary source is one document: 'EMAX MIDI and RS-422 specs, Copyright E-MU Systems 1986, Valid for EMAX Software Rev. 3.0, 12/16/86' (Emulator Archive transcription, PDF author David Mercer, 1999). No open-source Emax editor/librarian was found to cross-check the layout (Edisyn, KnobKraft: none). Hardware confirmation exists only for #1A (micromoog's F0 18 02 1A 00 57 02 1F/29 xx F7 examples, sequencer.de 2010; Kenton Control Freak users). Requests (#00-#08), #1B, #1C, #12, #14, #17, #1E, #22 and SDS are per spec only.
Reply to a request for a key/level with no voice (#00/#03) is not specified -- could be no reply, zeros, or a reply for another voice. The driver reads the key maps first and skips 7F levels.

Velocity to Q: spec says 4 bits 0-15; the panel (AP 17) shows +15 down to -16. Either the raw byte is wider than documented (5-bit two's complement or offset 16) or the manual is wrong. Modelled 0-15 raw; test by reading it back after setting a negative value on the panel.
Original Key: spec says '6 bits, 0 to 87' (87 needs 7 bits). Assumed a full byte 0-87.

Display scalings are inferred from panel ranges, not stated: tuning 3 cents/step (-48..+45), attenuation 1.5 dB/step (0-46 dB), keyboard tracking 0.125/step (0.00-1.87), master tune 3 cents/step, arp tempo = BPM x 100 (4000-24000 = 40-240 BPM).
Envelope panel values: AP 12/14 text says 01-32, one AP 14 line says 00-32. Modelled raw 0-31 displayed +1.

MIDI controller numbers (preset params 40-45): spec '1 to 32: midi controller #'; manual says controllers 0-31 and the panel scrolls 'off, 00 to 33'. Assumed raw n = CC n-1, 33 = pitch wheel, 34 = channel pressure.
Arpeggiator codes: note value 0-9 and interval 0-15 are mapped in the order the manual lists them; harmony 0 = off is inferred.

Sample rate codes 3 (22.050 kHz) and 7 (44.100 kHz) are in the Rev 3.0 spec but not in the v2.0 manual's six panel rates; whether an Emax I plays them correctly is untested. soundprogramming.net lists the Emax 'max sample rate 27,778 Hz' (likely the default rate).
Master tune values 0-15 are buggy on Rev 3.0 per the spec itself ('should be fixed next rev').

Execute Copy Preset (#17): the spec does not say whether an existing destination preset is overwritten silently (Create Preset #15 says it is). Also unclear whether the copy duplicates sample memory or shares it (the panel's copy-voice suggests voices become independent, which would consume sound RAM).

Whether voice edits via #1A are visible to OTHER presets that use the same voice: the manual implies voices belong to a preset (copied voices become 'a whole new voice for independent processing'), so edits should be local to the current preset.
SDS: channel byte expectations, behaviour on a null-voice dump request, and the secondary-voice sample number (key + 128 per this spec; the Emax II uses 256 + key) are unverified on hardware.

Dual Voice mode (PRESET DEFINITION 4) and voice names (voice params 54-59, 6 x 6-bit chars 'not used by EMAX at all', +32 = ASCII) exist but are not modelled: dual mode has no SysEx parameter, and the name chars are editor-only metadata.

Timing: no documented minimum gap or request latency; READY pacing is documented for changes only. The first message after a module change may be slow (OS overlays load from floppy). gapMs 20 and the timeouts in driverNotes are guesses.
OS 2.x behaviour: unknown whether it implements every command in this Rev 3.0 spec (3.0 added EEPROM support, reverse, more arp modes, MIDI analyzer per the Emulator Archive OS list).

Defaults in this schema are editor starting values taken from the manual's guided tours (Fc 100, Q 0, env 0, tracking 1.00, VCA S 32 R 05), not E-mu factory init values (the manual's Default Settings appendix is not in the transcription).
